page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server powered by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The system features 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 123.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, providing approximately 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is comprised of a 3890 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves a top-tier Passmark memory score, though large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is relatively weak, registering at 21.89 GB/sec. For lightweight AI workloads, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing and top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M parameter LLM models.

As a bare metal instance, this server offers dedicated hardware resources without virtualization overhead, making it highly resource-dense and cost-efficient for workloads requiring direct hardware access. The combination of a high-capacity 3890 GB NVMe SSD and 123.0 GB of DDR5 RAM makes it well-suited for database hosting, static web serving, and memory-intensive applications. However, the tradeoff of lower multi-core scaling and weaker large-block write bandwidth should be considered for highly parallelized write-heavy computing tasks.
